title: Calling 911 - Emergencies
objectives: Stay calm and follow dispatcher instructions
target_phrases: Can you send help right away?

dialogue.title: Emergency Call Practice
dialogue.context: Ahmed practices making a 911 call during a community safety class.

lines.speaker: Instructor
lines.text: Today we're practicing 911 calls. Remember: stay calm, speak clearly, and answer all questions.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: What if I'm too nervous to speak clearly?

lines.speaker: Instructor
lines.text: Take a deep breath. The dispatcher is trained to help you. They'll ask simple questions.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Okay, let's practice. I'll pretend there's a fire.

lines.speaker: Instructor
lines.text: Good. I'll be the dispatcher. Start your call.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Hello! I need help! There's a fire in my apartment building!

lines.speaker: Instructor
lines.text: Perfect! Is anyone hurt? Are you in a safe location?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Everyone is outside. We're all safe. Please send the fire department!

lines.speaker: Instructor
lines.text: Excellent! Fire trucks are on the way. Stay on the line. That was very good, Ahmed!

listening_exercises.transcript: Call 911 for life-threatening emergencies: fires, serious injuries, crimes in progress, or medical emergencies. For non-emergencies like noise complaints or minor car accidents with no injuries, call the non-emergency police number. Stay calm, speak clearly, and don't hang up until the dispatcher tells you it's okay.
listening_exercises.question: When should you call 911?

listening_exercises.transcript: When calling 911, the dispatcher will ask: What's your emergency? What's your location? Are you safe? Is anyone injured? Answer these questions clearly. The dispatcher might keep you on the phone to give first aid instructions or get more information. Don't hang up until they tell you it's okay.
listening_exercises.question: What should you do after answering the dispatcher's questions?
options: Wait for them to tell you it's okay to hang up

listening_exercises.transcript: If someone is unconscious and not breathing, tell the 911 dispatcher immediately. They'll guide you through CPR steps. For heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure with a clean cloth. For burns, run cool water over the area. The dispatcher will stay on the line and help until paramedics arrive.
listening_exercises.question: What will the dispatcher do if someone isn't breathing?

speaking_tasks.prompt: Practice a 911 call. Say: 'I need an ambulance! Someone fell and is bleeding. The address is [your address]. Please hurry!' Record yourself clearly.
speaking_tasks.example: 911, I need an ambulance! There's an emergency! Someone fell down the stairs and is bleeding from their head. The address is 8234 Southeast 82nd Avenue, Apartment 12. Please send help right away! Yes, they're breathing but not responding to me. Okay, I'll stay on the line.

speaking_tasks.prompt: Explain three types of emergencies when you should call 911. Talk for 30 seconds.
speaking_tasks.example: You should call 911 for serious emergencies. First, call if someone is badly hurt or unconscious. Second, call if there's a fire or you smell smoke. Third, call if you see a crime happening, like someone breaking into a house. Always stay calm and give your location clearly. Don't hang up until the dispatcher tells you it's okay.

writing_tasks.prompt: Write your address clearly, exactly as you would say it to a 911 dispatcher. Then write 3 sentences about why it's important to know your address in an emergency.
writing_tasks.example: My address is 8234 Southeast 82nd Avenue, Apartment 12, Portland, Oregon 97266. It's important to know your address in emergencies because the dispatcher needs to send help to the right place. If you don't know your address, help might not arrive in time. Everyone in your family should memorize your address.

writing_tasks.prompt: Write what you would say in this emergency: Your neighbor's house is on fire and people are trapped inside. (4-5 sentences)
writing_tasks.example: 911, there's a fire! My neighbor's house is on fire at 8236 SE 82nd Avenue. There are people trapped inside - I can hear them yelling for help! The fire is very big and coming from the back of the house. Please send fire trucks immediately! I'm outside and safe.

grammar_focus.title: Imperatives for Urgent Commands
grammar_focus.explanation: Use imperative (base verb) for urgent commands. No subject needed.

grammar_focus.title: Present Continuous for Current Emergencies
grammar_focus.explanation: Use present continuous (am/is/are + -ing) to describe what's happening NOW.

grammar_focus.title: There is/are for Describing Emergency Scenes
grammar_focus.explanation: Use 'There is/are' to describe what you see at the scene.

cultural_notes: 911 is the emergency number in the U.S. It's free to call from any phone.
You can call 911 from a cell phone even without service or a SIM card.
If you call 911 by mistake, don't hang up! Tell them it was an accident.
Most 911 centers have translation services for non-English speakers.
Teaching children to call 911 and know their address can save lives.
For non-emergencies, use the non-emergency police number (often 311 or local number).

dialogue: Maanta waxaan ku celcelinaynaa wicitaannada 911. Xusuuso: isdeg deg, u hadal si cad, kana jawaab su'aalaha oo dhan.
Ka warran haddii aan aad u walwalo in aan si cad u hadlo?
Neefso qoto dheer. Qofka wicitaanka qaada waa tababaran yahay inuu ku caawiyo. Waxay ku weydiin doonaan su'aalo fudud.
Hagaag, aan tababarno. Waxaan iska dhigayaa in dab jiro.
Waa hagaag. Anigu waxaan noqon doonaa qofka wicitaanka qaada. Bilaabi wicitaankaaga.
Hello! Caawimaad baan u baahanahay! Dab baa ka kacay daarta aan ku noolahay!
Waa fiican! Ma jirtaa qof dhaawacmay? Ma waxaad ku sugantahay meel ammaan ah?
Qof walba wuu banaanka yahay. Dhammaanteen waanu nabad qalnaa. Fadlan soo dir dab-demiska!
Waa aad u fiican! Gawaarida dab-demiska ayaa imanaya. Ha ka bixin xariiqda. Aad baad u fiicnaatay, Ahmed!

listening.question: Maxaad tahay inaad samayso ka dib markaad ka jawaabto su'aalaha qofka wicitaanka qaada?
Maxuu samayn doonaa qofka wicitaanka qaada haddii qof uusan neefsanayn?

speaking.instruction: Ku celi wicitaanka 911. Dheh: 'I need an ambulance! Someone fell and is bleeding. The address is [your address]. Please hurry!' Si cad isu duub.
Sharax saddex nooc oo xaalado degdeg ah oo ay tahay inaad wacdo 911. Ku hadal 30 ilbiriqsi.

writing.instruction: Qor cinwaankaaga si cad, sida aad u sheegi lahayd qofka 911. Kadib qor saddex jumlood oo ku saabsan sababta ay muhiim u tahay inaad ogaato cinwaankaaga xaalad degdeg ah.
Qor waxa aad dhihi lahayd xaalad degdeg ah: Guriga deriskaaga waa gubanaya, dad ayaa gudaha ku xayiran. (4-5 jumlood)

sections.explanation: U adeegso qaabka amarka (fal aasaasi ah) amarrada degdegga ah. Mawduuc looma baahna.

Istcmaal 'There is/are' si aad u sharaxdo waxa aad ku aragto goobta.
